Records every array that reaches it, and sends back any recorded frame on request.

A tape recorder for data. Capture a passage of movement, a gesture, a run of camera frames or analysis results, then replay it - slower, faster, backwards, scrubbed by hand or looped - or save it to a .npy file and bring it back in another session.

RECORDING:
Every message arriving at 'data to record' is turned into an array, copied, and added to the end of the recording. The node has no record switch of its own - put a gate in front of it, as the demo does. Frames only accumulate, so a second take goes after the first unless you click 'clear' first.

PLAYING BACK:
Send a frame number to 'current frame', or drag it, and the node sends that frame from 'data out'. Count through the numbers to play; send any number to jump straight to that frame. Frames count from 0. A number below 0 or past the last frame sends nothing. While recording, current frame shows the number of the frame just recorded (without sending it).

SYNTAX:
np.sequence
No arguments.

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

data to record:
Anything that can become an array. Each arrival is one frame.

current frame (drag int, also an inlet):
Which frame to send. Starts at -1 (nothing).

clear (button, also an inlet):
Empties the recording and sets current frame back to -1. Send it anything.

save (button):
Opens a save dialog and writes the whole recording as one .npy file, frames along the first axis. All frames should be the same shape.

load (button):
Opens a file dialog, REPLACES the recording with the file's frames (first axis = frames) and sets current frame back to -1.

path (option):
A .npy file to load. Setting it loads the file, so a patch that saves the path comes back with its recording.

OUTPUTS:

data out:
The frame asked for.

READING THE DEMO:
The patcher make_roving_circle makes the pictures: a 12 x 12 bright spot that circles the square once every 2.4 seconds (open it to see how). Its left outlet is the live picture, shown in the upper heat_map ten frames a second. Its middle outlet is the frames to record, and its right outlet clears the recording.

Click the button at the top left to record: the recording is cleared and the next 24 frames - one full circle, a frame every 15 degrees - go into np.sequence, then recording stops by itself.

The lower heat_map is what np.sequence sends back. The metro and counter play the 24 frames five a second - the spot goes round at half the live speed, and keeps going after recording has stopped, because it is reading the recording.

Switch the metro off and drag the slider to jump to any frame: frame 0 and frame 12 show the spot on opposite sides. Click the button again for a new take.

RELATED:
np.rolling_buffer keeps only the latest frames, continuously - a moving window rather than a recording. np.load reads a .npy file in one piece. np.grid and np.linalg.norm build the moving spot inside make_roving_circle.
